name: Viruses That Jumped: From Animals to People
description: From the first virus found in tobacco leaves to flu, Ebola, HIV, SARS and COVID-19: how infections cross between animals and people, and how we fought back.

checkpoints.name: Finding the invisible
checkpoints.note: In 1898 the tobacco mosaic virus was shown to cause disease in a plant, the first virus identified. The 1918 influenza pandemic killed millions, electron microscopes later let scientists see viruses, the polio vaccine arrived in 1955, and the WHO was created in 1948.

checkpoints.name: Flu waves and new viruses
checkpoints.note: The Asian flu of 1957 and the Hong Kong flu of 1968 were pandemic influenza. Ebola was recognised in Africa in 1976, and smallpox, long a scourge, was driven out by vaccination, with global eradication declared in 1980.

checkpoints.name: The HIV era
checkpoints.note: HIV/AIDS became a global pandemic after 1981. The virus is closely related to viruses found in African apes, and its spread showed how an infection that crosses between species can go round the world.

checkpoints.name: SARS and swine flu
checkpoints.note: SARS spread from China in 2002 and 2003 and was contained, the 2009 swine flu pandemic was a new influenza strain, and the cattle plague rinderpest was declared eradicated in 2011.

checkpoints.name: Ebola, Zika and COVID-19
checkpoints.note: West Africa suffered a large Ebola epidemic from 2013, and Zika was linked to birth defects. COVID-19 became a global pandemic in 2020, and mRNA vaccines were developed within a year.
